The One Everyone Talks About

The Lafayette Coney

A steamed bun, an all beef frank with a real snap, a ladle of house chili, a stripe of yellow mustard, and a pile of fresh diced onions. That is the Detroit order, and it has not needed changing since 1924.

Add fries on the side. Always.

How to order: Tell the counter how many, and how you want them. With everything means chili, onions, and mustard. MENU ITEMS ONLY • ASK AT THE COUNTER FOR TODAY'S DETAILS

Photos show classic Detroit coney style servings. Items and availability can vary by day.

Our Story

A Century at
One Counter

Lafayette Coney Island opened in 1924 on West Lafayette Boulevard in downtown Detroit. In a city that takes its coneys seriously, Lafayette kept it simple and kept it consistent. A quick counter, an open grill you can watch from the sidewalk, and a coney built the same way, order after order, decade after decade.

After renovations, Lafayette reopened in March 2025, refreshed and ready for the next century, with the same name over the door and the same job to do: feed downtown, fast and right.
